10.1002_adfm.78984: The fundamental trade‐off between structural stability and high capacity remains a key challenge in Li‐ion battery cathode design, especially in cost‐sensitive, large‐scale applications. Here, we present a spatially integrated intercalation–conversion hybrid cathode that combines LiFePO 4 and sulfur‐based materials within a monolayer architecture. This earth‐abundant composition synchronizes Li‐ion intercalation with the solid‐liquid sulfur conversion reaction: LiFePO 4 serves as a mechanically robust Li host and a chemical regulator that suppresses polysulfide shuttles, while sulfur‐based materials provide high specific capacity. By rationally tailoring the cathode composition and electrolyte solvation chemistry, we reveal how electrolyte–cathode synergistic interactions govern active material utilization, interfacial kinetics, and long‐term stability. The optimized Li‐metal battery delivers stable cycling over 3000 cycles with a low‐capacity decay rate of 0.016% per cycle at 5 C and also demonstrates stable cycling under practical asymmetric cycling protocols. This work provides a new design principle for hybrid cathodes, offering a scalable pathway toward ultra‐durable and high‐capacity Li‐metal batteries.
10.1021_acsami.6c13404: Polyaniline (PANI) holds promise as cathode material for energy-saving electrochromic windows due to its reversible optical modulation and intrinsic energy storage capability. However, the simultaneous realization of large-area electrode fabrication, high electrochromic performance, and superior energy storage remains a key challenge for PANI-based electrochromic windows. Herein, we report a scalable and facile approach to fabricate a PANI/carbon nanotube (CNT)/PANI composite film on transparent conductive glass through combination of chemical oxidation polymerization and spray coating. The introduction of a CNT interlayer, low-temperature polymerization of PANI, and dual-cathode design collectively endows the hybrid structure with enhanced electrical conductivity, accelerated ion diffusion, and increased active sites. The resulting Zn-ion electrochromic device delivers a high optical modulation of 82.3% at 650 nm, a low coloration transmittance of 5.4%, fast switching speeds (coloration/bleaching time: 5.8 s/4.6 s), and a neutral tint in the colored state. Notably, the device also exhibits attractive energy storage performance with a specific capacitance of 45.6 mF cm-2 and an energy density of 12.4 μWh cm-2. Under simulated solar irradiation, the electrochromic window achieves an optical power modulation of 67.3% and enables a temperature regulation of 6.6 °C by switching between transparent and colored states. As a proof of concept, a large-area prototype (10 × 10 cm2) demonstrating uniform color change and good adhesive stability is presented. This work provides a scalable and effective route toward high-performance, conducting polymer-based electrochromic windows for intelligent thermal management and on-site energy recovery, contributing to sustainable energy utilization and building energy efficiency.
10.1039_d5ta09731b: Employing a dual-monomer synergistic strategy, a wide-bandgap, high- polarity polyimide is constructed. The derived film achieves a discharge energy density of 2.68 J cm −3 with >90% efficiency at 200 °C, showing superior thermal-dielectric stability.
